newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Consob outlines new stock market rules.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Consob outlines new stock market rules.

text.p: Italy's stock market authority Consob has issued new guidelines, to become law in the next few days, which will pave the way for the full implication of the cross-border share trading Eurosim directive in Italy.

Italy embraced the Eurosim directive on September 1 this year to allow big investment banks outside Italy to become members of the Milan stock exchange and be able to compete directly with Italy's licenced brokers or Sims.
But in Italy, the full details surrounding the implementation of the Eurosim are still being finalised.
These new regulations will become law for a full year and after that Consob will reserve the right to make changes, a Consob statement said on Monday.
In the regulations, Consob is encouraging a high degree of concentration of share trading on the Milan bourse, but will still allowed trading outside the bourse under certain circumstances.
The Consob regulations will allow off the bourse trading if clients want this type of trade, if the price is better than on the bourse and also if the client is from outside Italy.
It also added that off bourse trading could be conducted if in block trades, or if the trade is in state-guaranteed bonds.
